dedupe_keys.name: noaa swpc geoelectric field models us canada 1d and empirical emtf 3d conus 1 minute maps

description: These near real-time maps give the geoelectric field in millivolts per kilometre induced at the ground during geomagnetic storms, a measure of the induction hazard to long conductors such as power lines, from which the induced current is estimated by integrating along the line. The US-Canada-1D model covers the lower 48 states and Canada up to 60 degrees latitude on a 0.5 degree grid, interpolating observatory magnetic data with Spherical Elementary Current Systems and convolving it with one-dimensional physiographic conductivity profiles (EPRI 2020 for the US, Trichtchenko et al. 2019 for Canada); the empirical EMTF 3D model, operational since fiscal year 2020, uses magnetotelluric transfer functions for the continental US where surveys exist and is recommended there. The product is a joint effort of NOAA SWPC and NRCan with the USGS and NASA CCMC, using USGS and NRCan observatories. Maps are accessible online on the SWPC page and as one-minute JSON files in the services.swpc.noaa.gov directory, free and public domain as US government data. Caveats: SWPC states the maps need further validation against measured fields or GIC, the 1D approximation can be substantially inaccurate in some regions, and it advises caution in operational mitigation without a validation study. It supports space weather hazard exposure and GIC simulation for power grids and pipelines; related records are NOAA SWPC products, INTERMAGNET and the WAPA neutral blocking device case study.
